files.purpose: Implements the Claude Code provider as a `@MainActor final class ClaudeSession: ProviderSession`: it launches the `claude` CLI in headless print mode with stream-json on both stdin and stdout (`-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio`), drives the CLI's control_request/control_response protocol (initialize, set_permission_mode, set_model, interrupt, stop_task) and turns the CLI's `system`, `stream_event`, `assistant`, `user`, `result` and `rate_limit_event` lines into the app's `ProviderEvent`s. Tool permission prompts (`can_use_tool`) become approval cards, AskUserQuestion becomes a question sheet and ExitPlanMode becomes a plan card, and Claude tool names are mapped to typed `ToolCall` rows. With Hydra on it either defines native heads (`--agents`, `--forward-subagent-text`, a per-head `StreamState` keyed by `parent_tool_use_id`, head events wrapped in `.agentEvent`) or, for heads on another provider, removes Claude's own `Agent`/`Task` tools. At the end of each turn it reports context usage and, new in 1.6.2, a `TokenSpend` event (`.tokenSpend`) alongside the TokenLedger total. A static `handshake` starts a bare, non-persisting CLI only to read its model list and slash commands.

Otherwise message.uuid is emitted as .assistantMessageID; text/thinking blocks complete the oldest open streamed id for that message id (FIFO) or a fresh "<messageID>-text-<UUID>" / "<messageID>-thinking-<UUID>"; TodoWrite becomes .todos; other tools emit .toolStarted and .toolUpdated with title, detail, edits and kind.

""` (line 552), and toolNames is shared with the heads and cleared at every lead result (line 591). A background head's tool_result that arrives after the lead's result therefore finds name "" and is not filtered by hiddenResultTools, so for example a head's TodoWrite result is emitted as `.toolUpdated` for an id that never had a `.toolStarted`.

Then `let isError = message["is_error"]?.bool ?? Approval requests (can_use_tool): tool name default "Tool"; AskUserQuestion questions use the question text as id, header default "", choices from options label/description, allowsMultiple from multiSelect (default false), allowsOther true, isSecret false. Others: kind .command for command tools, .fileChange for edit tools, else .tool; detail is request.description for commands, else the call detail; reason is decision_reason; toolItemID is tool_use_id. For a name that toolCall maps to nil, the fallback is `ToolCall(kind: .other, title: name)` (line 657): kind .tool, title the raw tool name, detail nil.

unresolved_questions: TokenSpend's full initializer and defaults (agentID etc.) and how the `.tokenSpend` event is consumed; defined outside this file.
TokenSpend.model can carry "default" when the user picked the default model, since `model` stores input.model verbatim; whether consumers map that is not visible here.

files.purpose: Implements the Codex provider as a `@MainActor final class CodexSession: ProviderSession` that drives `codex app-server` over JSON-RPC (a `JSONRPCConnection` on a `StdioProcess`, initialize with clientInfo "droppy-code"/"Droppy Code"). Per session it starts or resumes a thread with approval/sandbox policy, Hydra and MCP config, starts turns, interrupts, compacts, and rolls back conversations (thread/rollback, falling back to thread/fork plus archive), and it maps app-server notifications and server requests (command/file/permission approvals, user-input questions, MCP elicitation) to ProviderEvents, treating child threads as Hydra heads. Static helpers open throwaway connections to list skills as slash commands, list models, read plan rate-limit windows and banked reset credits, and consume a reset credit. New in 1.6.2, every observed token spend on the lead or a head is recorded through `recordCodexSpend`, which keys the ledger by rollout (thread) id and emits a `.tokenSpend` event naming the model and head.

rollback (lines 175-222): 30 s watchdog closes the connection; pages "thread/turns/list" (cursor, "limit": 100, "sortDirection": "desc", "itemsView": "notLoaded") counting turns newest-first up to and including targetID, and records the next older turn as previousID; stops when previousID is found or no cursor remains; repeated cursor is an error. Then "thread/rollback" with "numTurns": count; the answer must keep the same thread id, not contain the target, and end with previousID. RPCError containing "paginated threads do not support thread/rollback" switches to forkHistory. On success turnID = nil and the same threadID is returned.

forkHistory: without previousID (target was the oldest turn) archives the original thread, clears threadID and turnID, returns nil. Otherwise "thread/fork" with threadParameters + threadId, "lastTurnId": previousID, "excludeTurns": true; the new id must differ; verifies with "thread/turns/list" limit 1 desc that the newest turn is previousID; archives the original; on any failure archives the fork (errors ignored) and rethrows; adopts the new id and activeModel = result.model or the old one.

Both .tokenSpend (from recordCodexSpend) and .agentProgress go through onEvent directly and are not wrapped in .agentEvent.

TokenLedger.record(codexSpend:rolloutID:) (TokenLedger.swift:122-126) lowercases the id (`rolloutID.lowercased()`) and adds the spend to `state.liveCodex[...]` as well as the day, so the history scan can subtract it. turn/completed: status "interrupted" -> .interrupted, "failed" -> .failed, else .completed; error = errorMessage(turn.error) unless null. Lead: turnID nil, failed with usage-limit text emits .usageLimit, then .turnCompleted. Head: headTurns cleared, .agentFinished(summary: error). serverRequest/resolved removes the pending request and emits .requestResolved. thread/compacted -> info "Context compacted.". A failed lead turn with a null or absent turn.error emits `.turnCompleted(status: .failed, error: nil)`: there is no fallback text, unlike Claude's "Claude stopped before finishing.".

headStarted: ignores missing ids, unknown lead, or known heads. A thread whose parentThreadId is the lead is a head; otherwise it is taken as a head only when it has agentNickname or agentRole, with an OSLog notice. Both paths store headModels[id] = thread.model and emit .agentStarted with preview-based description and model.

itemStarted: agentMessage -> messageDelta with item text; reasoning -> empty reasoningDelta; plan -> planDelta; userMessage on a head re-emits .agentStarted with its brief (single line 80) as description and full text as prompt; hookPrompt/functionCallOutput/contextCompaction ignored; others emit toolStarted if mapped, and collabAgentToolCall registers heads at start. itemCompleted: agentMessage -> messageCompleted; reasoning -> summary parts joined by blank line, else content parts; plan -> planCompleted; others emit toolStarted + toolUpdated and always call describeHeads.

describeHeads: collabAgentToolCall with tool "spawnAgent" routes to a Hydra profile only when exactly one native routable profile matches item model and reasoningEffort; each receiverThreadIds entry is registered and announced with toolUseID item.id. subAgentActivity registers unknown agentThreadId heads (logged) and, for kind "completed"/"interrupted", clears the head turn and emits .agentFinished. Heads registered here get no headModels entry, so their spend events carry no model. Ordering consequence: a receiver registered here first is inserted into headThreads without a headModels entry (lines 771-773); a later thread/started for the same id then hits the `!headThreads.contains(id)` guard in headStarted (line 678) and returns, so headModels is never filled and that head's .tokenSpend has model nil. When thread/started came first, headModels is already set and describeHeads leaves it. Also, `.agentStarted` is emitted again for every receiver each time describeHeads runs for a spawnAgent item, which is at item/started (line 723) and again at item/completed (line 747).

B1->B2: file grew from 1034 to 1052 lines. (1) New `headModels: [String: String]` (lines 49-51), filled in both branches of headStarted (lines 688 and 695) from thread.model. (2) resetDate's ISO 8601 parsing, which built an ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] and fell back to a plain ISO8601DateFormatter, is replaced by `ISO8601.date(from: text)` (line 472), which ISO8601.swift:19-21 defines as `(try? fractional.parse(text)) ?? (try? plain.parse(text))` over `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true)` and `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()`: the same two shapes (fractional and whole-second internet date-time) are tried in the same order. (3) In thread/tokenUsage/updated, the four `TokenLedger.shared.record(spend:)` calls (the lead's fallback previously recorded `used` with no positive check) became `recordCodexSpend(...)` with rolloutID threadID/model activeModel for the lead and rolloutID head/model headModels[head]/agentID head for heads (lines 609, 611, 616, 621, 623). This changes ledger behaviour: B1 recorded every Codex spend, including a lead spend while threadID was nil, through `record(spend:)`; B2 records nothing in the ledger without a rollout id (only the .tokenSpend event goes out), and with one it calls `record(codexSpend:rolloutID:)`, which lowercases the id and adds the spend to `state.liveCodex` so the history scan subtracts it. (4) New `recordCodexSpend`: doc comment lines 662-667, declaration and body lines 668-674, using `TokenLedger.shared.record(codexSpend:rolloutID:)` and emitting `.tokenSpend`. (5) `.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` replaced by `.trimmed` at lines 689, 698, 770 and 808; Text.swift:132 defines `trimmed` as exactly that call, so no behaviour change.
unresolved_questions: How the TokenLedger history scan subtracts `state.liveCodex` from each rollout file's growth is outside this file and TokenLedger.swift:122-126 (the part read here only shows the lowercased id being added to liveCodex).

Lead spend with threadID nil: send(), compact() and rollback() all guard `let threadID` (lines 130, 171, 176), so no new turn can start after forkHistory archived the only thread (lines 269-273 set threadID and turnID to nil). A nil threadID can still be seen by notifications of a turn already in flight at that moment, or by notifications that arrive during start() before threadID is assigned (lines 95 and 104); all of them are routed to the lead (lines 538-539), their spend is emitted as .tokenSpend but not recorded in the ledger, and headStarted returns early (line 678). How often the app-server sends such notifications is not visible here.

Whether leaving heads registered by describeHeads or subAgentActivity without a headModels entry (so their .tokenSpend has model nil, even though spawn items carry item.model) is intended is not stated in the source.
